```json
{"ranking": ["M5", "M6", "M1"], "fault": "Tail current source M5 is undersized (W too small, so the M5:M6 mirror ratio is ~2.3 instead of ~5). The tail current is only about 22 uA."}
```

Too little tail current is consistent with every failure:

- **Low UGBW.** The input-pair gm is about 21.9 × 11.1 µA ≈ 243 µS. Then gm/(2π·2 pF) ≈ 19 MHz, which matches the simulated 18.9 MHz. Reaching 43 MHz needs roughly 2.2× the gm, so roughly 2.2× the current.
- **Slow settling.** Slew is limited to about 22 µA / 2 pF ≈ 11 V/µs (8.75 V/µs measured), which pushes settling to 67 ns.
- **M5 at the edge of saturation.** M5 has Vdsat ≈ 0.21 V with only 0.042 V of margin. A narrow device is being forced to carry its current.
- **Oversized input pair.** M1/M2 are 36 µm wide and biased deep in weak inversion. That sizing only makes sense if they were meant to carry more current.

The +20% sensitivities point the same way: making M5 wider raises UGBW and shortens settling.

M6 is the second suspect, because widening it would cause the same ratio error. I rank it lower because the M5 saturation symptom points at M5 itself.
